protections: mj-include targets must stay inside the include root (the filePath directory, or cwd if filePath is not set); the parser reads any resolved path today
include resolution in the CLI watcher (a separate implementation) must apply the same containment before it reads a file

traps.reason_to_dismiss: each recursion level checks against its own cwd, so a single-level test passes
watch-mode dependency scanner only; it never puts file content into the output
validate mode only reports errors, and the fix is assumed to live in mjml2html
a diagnostic comment, and the read already failed
extension is documentation, not a security boundary

trap_notes.T1: handleInclude resolves the attribute path with path.resolve(cwd, file) and reads it with no check that it stays under the root
trap_notes.T2: nested includes re-enter MJMLParser with filePath set to the partial, so cwd moves to the partial's directory; a root recomputed per call lets each level climb further
trap_notes.T3: the path is URI-decoded, then resolved; absolute paths ignore cwd entirely, and a string-prefix check on resolved paths would accept sibling directories that share the prefix (and symlinks are not realpath-ed)
trap_notes.T4: the CLI watcher uses its own include resolver (regex + path.join), which reads any referenced file and adds it to chokidar's watch list, with no containment
trap_notes.T5: CLI -v calls MJMLParser directly without filePath, so a guard placed only in mjml-core is skipped; a parser-level guard closes it
trap_notes.T6: the include root must be the configured filePath (CLI --config.filePath / .mjmlconfig), which may differ from the input file's directory; over-hardening to the input directory breaks the documented partials override
trap_notes.T7: a failed include writes the absolute resolved path into the HTML comment and the validator message, which works as an existence oracle
trap_notes.T8: the docs say includes must be .mjml, but the parser enforces no extension and the CLI test /.mjml/ is unanchored with an unescaped dot

masking: T2 shows only after a single-level containment check is added for T1

conflicts.what: rooting containment at the input file's directory (or cwd) breaks the documented --config.filePath partials directory and the parser test that includes ./test/incl.mjml relative to filePath '.'
a fixed root must be carried through recursion, but sub-partials that include siblings relative to their own directory must still resolve
the parser includes extensionless or other-extension partials today (no extension check at index.js:69); enforcing .mjml may break existing templates

fairness_risks: legitimate templates use '../partials/x.mjml' when filePath points at a subdirectory; a blanket '..' ban contradicts the filePath override (packages/mjml-cli/README.md:104-110)
default filePath '.' means the root is process.cwd(); tests must say whether cwd is the boundary (packages/mjml-parser-xml/src/index.js:37,48)
T7 and T8 are outside the advisories' stated CWE-36 scope; hidden tests for them need the report to mention them

design.why: These are three independent fix sites: the parser containment (T1 + T2, with T6 as the must-keep-working filePath root, which is the mimo trap), the separate CLI resolver (T4, deepseek type, dismissible as watch-only), and the path-leaking error node (T7, deepseek type, dismissible as diagnostic). Each has a different reason to dismiss. T2 can replace T6 as the mimo test inside group 1. T5 and T3 add nothing independent once the guard sits in the parser.

unverified: the pinned tree is mjml 4.6.2 (packages/mjml-parser-xml/package.json:4), before fix A (30e29ed2cdae); what A and B changed was not checked against git, so a_fix_leaves_b_open and b_in_code_a_wrote are left null
whether B's published fix enforces the .mjml extension or covers the CLI fileContext resolver (T4, T8)
whether chokidar watching an out-of-root path has any observable effect beyond a recompile trigger (T4 impact)
symlink escape (T3) was inferred from path.resolve without realpath; not exercised
